topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: I took a drag on my cigarette, the embers glowing like a distant lighthouse beacon. The rain was coming down, slicking the streets, but the sky couldn't wash away the memories. There was a tree, once, a sapling planted with the naivety of childhood by my own hands. It was a piece of the past, a totem of time passed. But now, it's gone, cut down to the stub of a memory. They say progress can't be stopped, that the city needs to breathe and grow. But in that missing gap where the tree stood, it's hard to see the sense. I walked away, the pavement echoing with each step, the city a canvas of grays, as always. But something felt different, a new layer of grit on an already tarnished soul. The world moves on, but not without a cost.
